messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: scale_fill_grey on a coxcomb plot
parts:
Hi All,

I'm fiddling with the examples in the help file for coord_polar. When
I add scale_fill_grey to a pie or bullseye plot, they turn grey as
expected. But the Coxcomb plot seems to ignore it. What am I doing
wrong?

Thanks,
Bob

# This does a pie and it accepts scale_fill_grey
pie <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(1), fill = factor(cyl))) +
geom_bar(width = 1)
pie + coord_polar(theta = "y") +
scale_fill_grey(start=.15, end=.85)

# This does a bullseye and it too accepts scale_fill_grey
pie <- ggplot(mtcars,
aes(x = factor(1), fill = factor(cyl))) +
geom_bar()
pie + coord_polar() + scale_fill_grey(start=.15, end=.85)

# Coxcomb ignores scale_fill_grey
cxc <- ggplot(mtcars,
aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
geom_bar(width = 1, colour = "black")
cxc + coord_polar() + scale_fill_grey(start=.15, end=.85)

messages.subject: Re: scale_fill_grey on a coxcomb plot
parts:
On Sat, Aug 20, 2011 at 4:42 PM, Bob <muen...@tennessee.edu> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I'm fiddling with the examples in the help file for coord_polar. When
> I add scale_fill_grey to a pie or bullseye plot, they turn grey as
> expected. But the Coxcomb plot seems to ignore it. What am I doing
> wrong?

Scales determine how an aesthetic mapping is applied, but they don't
set the mapping in the first place. In your third example you never
map fill to a variable, so there is no fill aesthetic for
scale_fill_grey to apply to. Try

# Coxcomb with scale_fill_grey
cxc <- ggplot(mtcars,
aes(x = factor(cyl), fill = factor(cyl))) +
